biological_reference.closest_mechanism: dACC conflict monitoring recruiting upstream cognitive control (Botvinick et al. 2001; Shenhav et al. 2013 EVC), with the decision variable taken as a near-tie margin between top options (Hanes & Schall 1996).
dependencies: a conflict signal on a normalised or adaptively-calibrated scale
a recruitment threshold that tracks the ambient distribution rather than a fixed constant
a downstream control resource whose recruitment actually changes the competing evaluation
biological_reference.divergence: The first dependency is unmet in the implementation and that is this run's headline. Biological conflict monitoring adapts to the ambient difficulty distribution (the Gratton effect the driver itself cites is precisely a DEMONSTRATION of adaptive, history-dependent recruitment thresholds). REE's trigger compares a raw score difference to a hardcoded 0.05. This is a load-bearing biology divergence, not a caveat -- and unusually, REE already contains the fix: the SD-E3-CHANNEL-COMMENSURABILITY operator (MECH-439, ree_core/predictors/e3_selector.py, IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-07) exists to normalise exactly the channel-scale monopoly that sets this margin's scale, and was OFF in this run.
biological_reference.lit_status: present -- the conflict-monitoring / EVC literature is cited at the call site and is adequate. No /lit-pull commission is owed.

learning_extracted: THE ONLY LOAD-BEARING CRITERION IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL, AND `outcome = "PASS"` IS ASSIGNED UNCONDITIONALLY. `criteria` contains exactly one entry, `C0_readiness_control_fires` (load_bearing: true, measured 1.0, threshold 1.0), which is the margin_threshold=1e6 guaranteed-fire burst. The driver's scoring block picks one of three measurement labels from `frac_seeds_recruited` and then assigns `outcome = "PASS"` on the next line regardless of which fired. So the verdict cannot vary with the science. This is a DEFENSIBLE design for a pure measurement diagnostic -- and it is precisely why a diagnostic PASS is never exempt from this skill, because to every downstream reader that does not open the driver, the manifest presents as a clean load-bearing PASS on a claim-tagged run.

RECRUITMENT IS SCALE-DETERMINED, NOT CONFLICT-DETERMINED -- the headline finding. The per-seed median E3 candidate-score margin spans 0.0183 (seed 5) to 11.16 (seed 1), a 609x range, against a FIXED absolute threshold of 0.05. Recruitment then follows the margin distribution almost deterministically: the per-seed fraction of margin samples at or below 0.05 is 0.856 / 0.197 / 0.160 / 0.022 / 0.011 / 0.010 / 0.010 and the corresponding fraction of episodes recruiting is 1.000 / 0.867 / 0.967 / 0.233 / 0.133 / 0.133 / 0.100. With ~12-15 fresh E3 evaluations per episode, a per-sample rate p predicts an episode rate of 1-(1-p)^13, which reproduces the four low-rate seeds to within a few points (p=0.011 -> 0.134 predicted vs 0.133 observed; p=0.022 -> 0.251 vs 0.233). So the DV is a near-deterministic readout of where an UNTRAINED random-init network's score scale happens to sit relative to a hardcoded constant.

THE DRIVER ANTICIPATED THE SCALE CONFOUND BUT PRE-COMMITTED IT TO ONE DIRECTION ONLY. Its red-team F1b/F2 note says, correctly, that 'a "dormant" reading alongside margins that sit far above 0.05 supports a scale/calibration reading; a "dormant" reading with margins hovering near 0.05 supports a genuine near-tie-rate reading.' Both clauses are conditioned on a DORMANT outcome. The observed outcome is ENGAGED -- and the confound is exactly as strong in that direction: the engaged verdict is carried entirely by the 3 of 7 seeds whose margins sit near the threshold, while the other 4 have median margins 32x to 223x the threshold and recruit in 10-23% of episodes. A pre-registered confound analysis that names only one of the two possible outcomes is a coin-flip away from not applying, and this run landed on the side it did not cover.

THE ROUTING STATISTIC DESTROYS THE RUN'S OWN MOST INFORMATIVE SIGNAL. The label routes on `frac_seeds_recruited` = the fraction of seeds with total_requests > 0 across 30 episodes -- a per-seed BINARY indicator whose bar is one request in thirty episodes. Observed 7/7 -> 'engaged'. But the underlying per-seed recruitment fractions are sharply BIMODAL (0.867, 0.967, 1.000 against 0.100, 0.133, 0.133, 0.233) with no seed in between, and that bimodality is the actual finding. The driver's red-team F3b was RIGHT that the seed is the independent sampling unit (a static untrained network makes within-seed episodes correlated draws) -- but the per-seed statistic it then chose is maximally insensitive: it collapses a 609x scale spread and a 10x recruitment-rate spread into a 1-bit-per-seed indicator. Correct diagnosis of the independence problem, wrong choice of the seed-level summary.

READOUT (a) IS ARITHMETICALLY CENSORED AT 2, AND THE MOST INFORMATIVE SEED IS PINNED ON IT. `mean_request_rate_per_episode` was introduced per red-team F1a specifically so it would be 'a genuinely distinct statistic' from the binary readout (b), with TICKS_PER_EPISODE raised from 20 to 100 to give '~9 eligible evaluations/episode'. But the trigger is debounced while a coalition of the same demand_type is already active (`_ect_already_active`, ree_core/agent.py), and `coalition_max_duration_ticks` defaults to 50 -- so 100 ticks per episode admits AT MOST 2 requests, whatever the demand. The manifest confirms the bound exactly: across all 210 episodes the per-episode request count is 0, 1 or 2 and NEVER 3 (histogram 0:107, 1:51, 2:52), and seed 5 -- the seed with by far the most sub-threshold margins -- sits at exactly 2 in ALL 30 of its episodes. F1a's fix made (a) formally distinct from (b) but left it with a dynamic range of three values and a hard ceiling that the one high-demand seed saturates. The fix is to report requests per ELIGIBLE opportunity (requests / fresh-E3-results), or to raise TICKS_PER_EPISODE well above coalition_max_duration_ticks, not to raise ticks from 20 to 100 and stop.

EVALUATION OPPORTUNITY IS NOT EQUAL ACROSS SEEDS, AND NOTHING CONTROLS FOR IT. Every seed ran 30 episodes x 100 ticks, yet the number of FRESH E3 results (margin samples, de-duplicated by object identity so a latched read is never recounted) differs by seed: 390, 360, 450, 390, 390, 390, 360 -- 12.0 to 15.0 per episode, a 25% spread. Since recruitment is an at-least-once-per-episode event over those opportunities, the opportunity count feeds the recruitment rate independently of the margin distribution. It is small relative to the 609x scale effect and does not change any conclusion here, but a successor reporting rates per episode should normalise by opportunities or report the two separately.

ARC-131'S OWN MOTIVATING EXAMPLE IS NOW PARTLY STALE, AND THE CORRECTION IS A NARROWING RATHER THAN A DELETION. ARC-131's `notes` describe coalition control as an installability failure because REE 'has typed control demands, coalition templates and a controller, but it is inert until manually called and no endogenous monitor invokes it'. The second half is no longer true: chip-20260902-arc131-coalition-endogenous-recruitment-driver landed an endogenous monitor (ree-v3 88c7c3332c) and this run shows it firing in 7/7 seeds. But the example survives in a narrower and arguably more interesting form -- `use_endogenous_coalition_trigger` defaults to False (ree_core/agent.py line 803, `getattr(config, "use_endogenous_coalition_trigger", False)`) and exactly ONE driver in the whole ree-v3 experiments corpus enables it: this one. So the CAPABILITY now exists and the DEFAULT COMPOSITION still does not recruit it, which is precisely ARC-131's own distinction between a mechanism being possible and the whole agent entering the states in which it operates. Governance should refresh the note to that split rather than strike the example.

THE DRIVER CITES A claims.yaml FIELD THAT DOES NOT EXIST. Its lineage section says 'Its own blocked_note names coalition control (SD-091/MECH-481) as a concrete illustrative case.' ARC-131 has NO `blocked_note` key -- its keys are claim_level, claim_type, coupled_with, depends_on, epistemic_category, evidence, id, implementation_phase, live_status, notes, polarity, registered_utc, source, status, subject, title, version_relevance. The content is real and is in `notes`. Substantively harmless; procedurally not, because a governance reader following the citation finds nothing and may conclude the premise was invented.

RECORDING GAP, AND THIS ONE IS THE SERIOUS KIND: the manifest is missing BOTH `elapsed_seconds` AND `config` (`validate_recording.py`: 1 manifest, 2 always-core gaps). A missing `config` means the run is not reproducible from its own manifest and that the parameters which GENERATE the headline finding are not recorded -- `coalition_max_duration_ticks` (50, which sets the request ceiling), `e3_steps_per_tick` (10, which sets the evaluation cadence), GRID_SIZE/NUM_HAZARDS/NUM_RESOURCES, SELF_DIM/WORLD_DIM -- all of which this autopsy had to recover by reading ree_core and the driver source. Recording-debt, not measurement-debt: the fix is to call `stamp_recording_core` in the successor, never to re-run blind. Note this is the SECOND manifest in this staging batch missing always-core fields, which points at the shared emit path rather than at either author.

HYGIENE, recorded so a recompute does not look like a discrepancy: the manifest's `e3_margin_median` and `pooled_median_e3_margin` are computed as `sorted(x)[len(x)//2]`, the UPPER of the two middle order statistics, not the averaged median. Independent recomputation with an averaging median agrees to within 1.6% on every seed (e.g. seed 0: 0.138954 manifest vs 0.136772 recomputed; pooled: 0.578491 vs 0.578079). No conclusion depends on the difference. Separately, the pooled median across seeds whose scales differ by 609x is a mixture statistic with no clean interpretation, and should not be quoted as a summary of 'the' margin scale -- the per-seed medians are the meaningful figures and the manifest does record them.

A CORRECTED COUNT, AND THE MISCOUNT'S CAUSE, since the figure is quoted in the claim-facing note: exactly ONE driver in `ree-v3/experiments` enables `use_endogenous_coalition_trigger` (this one) -- that figure stands. But the companion figure for `use_coalition_controller` is FOUR real drivers (v3_exq_886, v3_exq_970, v3_exq_972, v3_exq_1038), not six: the first count included two `__pycache__/*.pyc` files. A recursive grep over an experiments tree counts compiled artifacts unless they are excluded, and a count quoted into a claim note is exactly where that must not happen. (Recorded also because the Step 7c red-team reported the ENDOGENOUS flag as enabled by two drivers including v3_exq_886; that is incorrect -- 886 sets only `use_coalition_controller` at its lines 526 and 901 and never the endogenous trigger. A red-team finding is a pointer to check, not a verdict, in this direction too.)

A `corrupting` SEVERITY FIELD DOES NOT IMPLY A LIVE GATE, AND THE GAP IS INVISIBLE FROM THE FIELD (Step 7c red-team F2). `f_dominance_conversion_ceiling` carries `severity: corrupting` and `status_phase: build_owed`, which reads as an open, gating, corrupting entry. It is not one: `check_substrate_path_overlap.py` -- the Step 2.5c gate -- decides OPEN vs CLOSED from the `status` STRING against a closed set including 'validated', and that entry's status is the long 'mech448_lead_lever_BUILT_VALIDATED_PROMOTED_provisional__...' token, which matches CLOSED. So the entry gates nothing and is absent from the gate's own open list. Generalisable rule for any autopsy leaning on an upstream entry: run the gate's script rather than reading the severity field, because the two disagree silently and in the direction that makes you believe you are protected when you are not. Handed to governance as a finding in its own right; not this autopsy's to fix.

THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS AUTOPSY'S OWN PRIMARY RECOMMENDATION WOULD HAVE PRODUCED AN INERT ARM (Step 7c red-team F4). It said to add `use_e3_channel_commensurability=True` as an arm without saying HOW. That flag is an `E3Config` field, and `REEConfig.from_dims` ends in a `**kwargs` sink its body never reads, so the natural spelling -- passing it to `from_dims` -- is silently dropped and the ON arm becomes bit-identical to the control. The autopsy would then have shipped, as its repair, the very defect class it was written to repair: an arm that cannot discriminate by construction. Two generalisable rules: (i) a recommendation to 'add an arm with flag X' must name the assignment PATH and a read-back readiness assert, never just the flag; (ii) for this config object specifically, the [memory] reference-reeconfig-from-dims-silent-kwargs rule applies to every new knob, and V3-EXQ-1012a's `cfg.e3.<flag> = True` plus `getattr(agent.e3.config, <flag>)` read-back is the pattern to copy.

routing_detail.requeue_rationale: Alphabetic suffix, not a new number: the scientific question -- does the endogenous coalition trigger engage at its shipped default in a live full-loop run, and how often -- is unchanged. What was wrong is the measurement's construction.
required_changes: MAKE THE SCALE AN ARM, NOT A NUISANCE -- AND SET THE FLAG ON THE PATH THAT ACTUALLY READS IT. Add a second arm with E3 channel-commensurability ON against the current default-off arm, holding everything else fixed. This converts the run's dominant uncontrolled variable into a measured one, and it simultaneously gives MECH-439's operator a consumer-side behavioural reading. Declared null: the cross-seed spread in per-seed recruitment fraction does not shrink under normalisation -- which would mean the 609x margin spread is not what drives recruitment after all. MECHANICAL WARNING, AND THIS IS LOAD-BEARING (Step 7c red-team F4): `use_e3_channel_commensurability` is an `E3Config` field (ree_core/utils/config.py:1073, default False), NOT a `REEConfig.from_dims` keyword. `from_dims` ends in a `**kwargs` sink (config.py:8408) that its body never reads, so passing the flag there is SILENTLY DROPPED with no error and the ON arm would be bit-identical to the control -- an arm inert by construction, which is exactly the defect class this autopsy is repairing. This is the known [memory] reference-reeconfig-from-dims-silent-kwargs failure mode, and config.py's own comments at 8374-8401 name it. Use the pattern V3-EXQ-1012a already uses: set `cfg.e3.use_e3_channel_commensurability = True` directly on the built config (1012a line 355), then READ IT BACK OFF THE LIVE OBJECT as a readiness assert -- `bool(getattr(agent.e3.config, 'use_e3_channel_commensurability', False))` (1012a line 357) -- and additionally assert the operator actually ENGAGED (its running channel-scale estimates left warm-up), not merely that the flag is set. A run whose ON arm silently equals its OFF arm must fail readiness, not report a null. STATE THE OPERATOR'S OWN STATUS in the driver: SD-E3-CHANNEL-COMMENSURABILITY is 'IMPLEMENTED but UNVALIDATABLE AS SPECIFIED' since the 2026-09-10 GFLAG-0234 amendment, so this arm exercises an operator whose own validation is open.

REPORT AND ROUTE ON A STATISTIC THAT CAN EXPRESS BIMODALITY. `frac_seeds_recruited` (fraction of seeds ever recruiting) must not be the routing statistic: its bar is one request in thirty episodes and it read 1.0 on a sharply bimodal distribution. Route on the per-seed recruitment-fraction DISTRIBUTION -- e.g. its median and spread, or the count of seeds above and below a declared rate -- and keep the ever-recruited fraction as descriptive context only. Keep red-team F3b's correct insight that the SEED is the independent unit; change only the seed-level summary.

REMOVE THE CEILING FROM READOUT (a). Report requests per ELIGIBLE OPPORTUNITY (requests divided by the seed's own count of fresh E3 results), which also fixes the unequal-opportunity problem below, and/or raise TICKS_PER_EPISODE well above `coalition_max_duration_ticks` (50) so the arithmetic maximum of 2 requests/episode is not reachable. Verify the fix worked by asserting no seed's per-episode count sits at the arithmetic maximum in every episode -- seed 5 did exactly that here.
NORMALISE OR REPORT EVALUATION OPPORTUNITY PER SEED. Fresh-E3-result counts ranged 360-450 across seeds at identical episode and tick budgets; a rate reported per episode inherits that 25% spread.

RECORD THE MARGIN DISTRIBUTION RELATIVE TO THE THRESHOLD, not only in absolute units -- per seed, report the fraction of samples below threshold alongside the median, since that fraction is what actually predicts recruitment (it reproduced the observed episode rates to within a few points here).

STAMP `config` AND `elapsed_seconds` via `stamp_recording_core` (Experimental Recording Standard 2026-07-12 section 3b). The missing `config` is what forced this autopsy to recover `coalition_max_duration_ticks` and `e3_steps_per_tick` from source.

STATE IN THE DRIVER THAT THE PASS CRITERION IS THE READINESS CONTROL AND CANNOT VARY WITH THE MEASUREMENT. The current design is defensible but the manifest does not say so; a `combination_rule` string of the kind V3-EXQ-1030's manifest carries would make it legible without changing any behaviour.
